rd-school-c1-english.revision-practice.title: Class 1 English: The Big Revision Book
rd-school-c1-english.revision-practice.subtitle: All ten units in one happy journey — feelings to friends!

sections.h: Me, my body and my day (Units 1–2)
sections.md:
**Greetings:** Good morning, Good afternoon, Good night, Hello, Namaste, Goodbye.

**Magic words:** please, thank you, sorry, excuse me.

**Feelings:** happy 😊, sad 😢, angry 😠, scared 😨, surprised 😮.

**My body:** eyes to see, ears to hear, nose to smell, tongue to taste, hands to touch.

**Clean habits:** bath every day — wet, rub soap, scrub, rinse, dry. Brush teeth morning and night. Wash hands before eating.

**Rhymes:** tub–rub–scrub.

check.q: Which is a magic word?
check.why: 'Please' is a polite magic word we use when we ask for something.

sections.md:
**Pets:** dog (woof), cat (meow), fish, rabbit, parrot. Pets need food, water, a home, love and a vet.

**Farm animals:** cow (moo), goat (baa), hen (cluck).

**Birds:** parrot, crow (caw), sparrow (chirp), peacock — our **national bird**. Birds have wings, feathers and a beak, and build nests.

**Little creatures:** ant, bee (makes honey), butterfly, snail, spider (spins a web). Butterfly life: egg → caterpillar → pupa → butterfly.

head: Animal
Sound
Where it lives
fig.caption: Animal sounds and homes.

check.q: Which bird is the national bird of India?
check.why: The peacock is India's national bird.

sections.md:
**Fruits:** mango (king of fruits), banana, apple, grapes, orange, guava, jamun.

**Tree parts:** roots (under the ground), trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits.

**Trees give:** fruit, fresh air, shade, wood, homes for birds.

**Seed → sprout → plant → tree.** Banyan is the **national tree**.

**One and many:** one apple, two apples; one leaf, many leaves.

check.q: Which part of a tree drinks water from the soil?
check.why: Roots take in water from the soil.

sections.md:
**Shapes:** circle (no corners), triangle (3 corners), square (4 equal sides), rectangle.

**Play words:** jump, hop, clap, run, ride.

**Kites** fly with the **wind**. We feel wind but cannot see it.

**Sky:** day — sun, clouds; night — moon, stars.

**Rain:** water rises, makes clouds, falls as rain — the water cycle. Monsoon is India's rainy season.

**Rainbow:** VIBGYOR — violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.

check.q: What does VIBGYOR help us remember?
check.why: VIBGYOR is the order of the seven rainbow colours.

sections.md:
**Community helpers:** doctor, teacher, police officer, farmer, postman, firefighter, sanitation worker, cook.

**At home** everyone helps — you too!

**Good friends** share, take turns, help, say sorry and listen.

**Helping words:** *Please help me. May I help you? Thank you.*

**Emergency in India: 112.**

check.q: Who brings letters and parcels?
check.why: The postman delivers letters and parcels.

sections.md:
Say the first sound of each word:

| Word | First sound |
|---|---|
| happy, hen | h |
| bath, bird, banana | b |
| mango, moon | m |
| tree, trunk | t |
| kite, king | k |
| sun, sky, snail | s |

**Rhyme families:** tub–rub, tree–bee, kite–white, sky–high, bug–hug.

**Opposites:** big–small, fast–slow, up–down, happy–sad, soft–hard.

check.q: Which word starts with the same sound as 'moon'?
check.why: 'Moon' and 'mango' both begin with the 'm' sound.

sections.md:
**Action words** tell what we do: *eat, drink, sleep, read, sing, dance, swim, fly.*

- The bird **flies**. The fish **swims**. The baby **sleeps**.

**Describing words** tell how things are: *big, small, red, yellow, hot, cold, tall, short.*

- A **big** elephant. A **small** ant. A **red** apple. A **hot** cup of tea.

**Where is it?** — *in, on, under.*

- The cat is **on** the mat. The ball is **under** the bed. The fish is **in** the bowl.

**Counting fun:** one sun, two eyes, three corners of a triangle, four legs of a cow, five fingers on a hand.

**Ask and answer:**

- *What is your name?* — *My name is ___.*
- *How old are you?* — *I am six.*
- *What colour is the sky?* — *The sky is blue.*

check.q: Where is the ball? 'The ball is ___ the bed.' (It is below the bed.)
check.why: When something is below another thing, we say it is 'under' it.

sections.md:
**Read and draw.** Read each line with a grown-up and draw it:

1. A yellow sun in a blue sky.
2. A green tree with three red apples.
3. A brown dog under the tree.
4. A kite flying high.

**Say a rhyme.** Choose one rhyme you learnt this year and say it with actions — clap, jump or wave your hands.

**Tell a story in three parts.** Use the words *first, then, at last*:

- *First* the seed was in the soil.
- *Then* rain fell and a sprout came up.
- *At last* it became a big tree.

**My favourite.** Finish the sentences:

- *My favourite fruit is ___.*
- *My favourite animal is ___.*
- *My favourite colour is ___.*

Well done! You have finished Class 1 English!

check.q: Which word tells what happens at the end of a story?
check.why: 'At last' tells us what happens at the end.

parts.md: On Monday Riya said *Good morning!* to everyone and took a splashy bath — rub, scrub, splash! On Tuesday she fed Motu the kitten and gave him fresh water. *Meow!* said Motu. That means *thank you* in cat language.

On Wednesday Mithu the parrot helped her find the ripest mango on the tree, and she shared it with her little brother. On Thursday she went to the mela and found circles on the giant wheel, squares on the sweet boxes and triangles on the flags.

On Friday she flew a yellow kite in the wind — up, up, high in the sky! On Saturday rain fell, *pitter-patter*, and then a rainbow came — VIBGYOR! On Sunday she helped Ma set the plates and thanked the postman uncle for her birthday card. *What a wonderful week!* said Riya. *I learned so much!*

summary: Greet people: Good morning, Hello, Namaste, Goodbye.
Magic words: please, thank you, sorry, excuse me.
Feelings: happy, sad, angry, scared, surprised.
Clean habits: daily bath, brush teeth, wash hands.
Pets need food, water, home, love and care.
Birds have wings, feathers, beak; peacock is national bird.
Tree parts: roots, trunk, branches, leaves, fruits.
Shapes: circle, square, triangle, rectangle.
Wind lifts kites; rain comes from clouds; rainbow is VIBGYOR.
Helpers: doctor, teacher, police, farmer, postman, firefighter.
Good friends share, take turns and help.
Action words, describing words and in–on–under help us talk.
Opposites and rhymes make English fun.

rd-school-c1-english.unit-1-happy-me.title: Happy Me: Feelings and Greetings
rd-school-c1-english.unit-1-happy-me.subtitle: Say hello, say thank you, and learn the names of your feelings!

sections.md:
Can you wave your hand? Wave it high! Wave it low!

When we meet someone, we **greet** them. A greeting is a kind word we say when we meet.

- In the morning we say **Good morning!**
- In the afternoon we say **Good afternoon!**
- At night we say **Good night!**
- Any time we can say **Hello!** or **Namaste!**

When Riya comes to school, she smiles at her teacher and says, *Good morning, Ma'am!* Her teacher smiles back. A greeting makes two people happy at the same time. That is a little bit of magic!

**Try it:** Turn to the child next to you. Smile. Say, *Hello! My name is ___.* Now listen to their name.

keyTerms: greet — say a kind word when you meet someone
Namaste — a greeting with folded hands

check.q: What do you say when you meet your teacher in the morning?
check.why: In the morning we greet people with 'Good morning!'

sections.md:
Some words are so kind that we call them **magic words**.

| When | Magic word |
|---|---|
| You want something | **Please** |
| Someone gives you something | **Thank you** |
| You make a mistake | **Sorry** |
| You need to pass by | **Excuse me** |

Aman wants a red crayon. He says, *Please may I have the red crayon?* Meena gives it. Aman says, *Thank you!* Meena says, *You are welcome!*

**Did you know?** In many Indian languages there are words for thank you: *dhanyavaad* in Hindi, *nandri* in Tamil, *dhonnobad* in Bangla.

check.q: Meena gives you a pencil. What do you say?
check.why: When someone gives us something, we say 'Thank you'.

sections.md:
Our face can show how we feel inside. Let us learn the names of feelings.

- 😊 **Happy** — I got a new ball!
- 😢 **Sad** — My ice cream fell down.
- 😠 **Angry** — Someone broke my toy.
- 😨 **Scared** — There was a loud thunder.
- 😮 **Surprised** — A gift for me?

All feelings are okay. When you feel sad or angry, you can **tell** someone: *I feel sad.* Then a grown-up can help you.

**Game:** Your teacher says a feeling. You make that face! Happy face... sad face... surprised face!

keyTerms: feeling — what you feel inside, like happy or sad

check.q: Your ice cream fell down. How might you feel?
check.why: Losing something we like can make us feel sad, and that is okay.

sections.md:
You are special! Let us talk about **me**.

- *My name is ___.*
- *I am ___ years old.*
- *I like ___.*
- *I am happy when ___.*

Say these lines aloud. Use a big, clear voice. Look at your friends when you speak.

**Sound fun:** *Happy* starts with **h**. Can you think of other words with h? *hat, hen, hand, house!*

**Draw:** Draw your face. Show how you feel today.

check.q: Which word begins with the same sound as 'happy'?
check.why: 'Hen' and 'happy' both begin with the 'h' sound.

sections.md:
When we leave, we say **Goodbye!** or **Bye-bye! See you tomorrow!**

At the end of school, Riya waves to her teacher: *Goodbye, Ma'am! See you tomorrow!* At bedtime she hugs her mother: *Good night, Ma!*

Now you know how to greet, how to use magic words and how to name your feelings. You are a **happy, kind** friend!

parts.md: Tara woke up and felt grumpy. Her sock was missing. Her hair was messy. *Hmph!* she said. She did not say good morning to anyone. Her little brother Golu said, *Good morning, Didi!* But Tara only frowned.
On the school bus, the driver uncle smiled. *Good morning, Tara!* Tara mumbled, *Good morning.* Uncle smiled even more. Something warm and sunny began to grow inside Tara.

In class, her friend Kabir said, *Hello, Tara! Please play with me?* Tara said, *Yes!* and they built a tall tower of blocks. When it fell, they both laughed. *Sorry!* said Kabir. *It's okay!* said Tara.
At home Tara hugged Golu. *Sorry I was grumpy, Golu. Good evening!* Golu giggled. That night Tara thought: a smile and a kind word can turn a grumpy day into a happy one. *Good night, everyone!*

summary: A greeting is a kind word we say when we meet someone.
Morning: Good morning. Afternoon: Good afternoon. Night: Good night.
Hello and Namaste can be said any time.
Magic words: please, thank you, sorry, excuse me.
Feelings have names: happy, sad, angry, scared, surprised.
All feelings are okay; we can tell a grown-up how we feel.
We can introduce ourselves: My name is…, I am … years old.
When we leave, we say goodbye.

glossary.d: say hello in a kind way
kind words like please and thank you

rd-school-c1-english.unit-10-helpers-fri.title: Helpers and Friends
rd-school-c1-english.unit-10-helpers-fri.subtitle: Who helps us every day — and how can we help too?

sections.md:
Many people help us every day. They are our **community helpers**.

| Helper | What they do |
|---|---|
| 👩‍⚕️ doctor | makes us well when we are ill |
| 👩‍🏫 teacher | helps us learn |
| 👮 police officer | keeps us safe |
| 🧑‍🌾 farmer | grows our food |
| 📮 postman | brings letters and parcels |
| 🧑‍🚒 firefighter | puts out fires |
| 🧹 sweeper / sanitation worker | keeps our streets clean |
| 🧑‍🍳 cook | makes tasty food |

**Say it:** *The farmer grows rice. The doctor helps sick people.*

fig.caption: A fire engine rushes to help; a doctor is ready.
fig.alt: An animated fire engine with a flashing light and a doctor.

keyTerms: community helper — a person whose work helps everyone around us

check.q: Who puts out fires?
check.why: A firefighter uses water and a fire engine to put out fires.

sections.md:
Every helper uses special **things** to do the work. Can you match them?

| Helper | Uses |
|---|---|
| doctor | stethoscope, medicine |
| teacher | book, chalk, board |
| farmer | plough, seeds, water |
| postman | bag, letters, cycle |
| firefighter | fire engine, water pipe, ladder |
| cook | pan, spoon, stove |
| tailor | needle, thread, scissors |
| barber | comb, scissors |

**Where do they work?**

- The doctor works in a **hospital** or clinic.
- The teacher works in a **school**.
- The farmer works in a **field**.
- The firefighter waits at the **fire station**.

**Game:** One child acts out a helper — maybe sweeping, or cooking, or giving a letter. Others guess: *Are you a cook? Are you a postman?*

check.q: What does a doctor use?
check.why: A doctor listens to our heartbeat with a stethoscope.

sections.md:
At home too, everyone helps.

- Ma cooks and goes to work.
- Papa washes the clothes and helps with homework.
- Dadi tells stories. Dada waters the plants.

And **you** can help! You can:

- put your toys back in the box
- fold your clothes
- set the plates for dinner
- water the plants

Work at home is for **everyone** — boys and girls, big and small.

check.q: How can you help at home?
options: put toys back in the box
check.why: Putting toys away is a simple way to help at home.

sections.md:
A **friend** is someone we like to play with. A good friend:

- **shares** toys and snacks
- **takes turns** on the swing
- **helps** when you fall
- says **sorry** after a mistake
- **listens** when you talk

You can be a good friend too. If a new child sits alone, go and say, *Hello! Do you want to play with us?*

Friends can be different. A friend may speak another language at home, eat different food, or use a wheelchair. We can all play together.

fig.caption: Two friends hold hands — friends share and care.
fig.alt: Two smiling children holding hands with a floating heart.

check.q: What does a good friend do on the swing?
check.why: Good friends take turns so everyone gets to play.

sections.md:
When we need help we say: *Please help me.* *Can you help me, please?*

When someone helps us: *Thank you for helping me!*

When we offer help: *May I help you?*

**Emergency:** If there is danger, tell a grown-up. In India you can call **112** for emergency help. Learn your home address and a parent's phone number.

**Rhyme:** *Help, help, I can help! Big or small, I help all!*

check.q: How do you offer help politely?
check.why: 'May I help you?' is a polite way to offer help.

sections.md:
**Talk time.** Sit in a circle. Each child says:

- *My friend's name is ___.*
- *We like to play ___.*
- *I help my ___ at home.*

**Sounds.** Say the first sound: **d**octor, **f**armer, **p**ostman, **t**eacher, **c**ook. Can you think of another word with the same first sound? (doctor — dog; farmer — fish)

**Make a thank-you card.** Fold a paper. Draw a helper you like — maybe the school guard, the bus driver or the vegetable seller. Write or copy: *Thank you!* Give it to the helper with a smile.

**Did you know?** Some helpers work at night while we sleep — nurses, police officers, train drivers and bakers who make fresh bread for the morning.

check.q: Which word starts with the same sound as 'farmer'?
check.why: 'Farmer' and 'fish' both begin with the 'f' sound.

parts.md: Raju was riding his bicycle to school. Bump! The wheel hit a stone. Raju fell and scraped his knee. His books flew everywhere. *Ouch!* said Raju, and a tear rolled down his cheek.

His friend Salma ran to him. *Are you okay?* She picked up his books. The traffic police uncle stopped the cars so they could cross safely. At school, the teacher cleaned his knee and put on a bandage. *Brave boy!* she said.

In the evening, the cycle repair uncle fixed his wheel. Raju thought, *So many people helped me today!* He made a card that said *Thank you* and drew a big sun on it. The next day, when little Mini dropped her lunch box, Raju was the first to help her pick it up. *Thank you, Raju bhaiya!* she smiled. Raju smiled too. Helping felt good!

summary: Community helpers make life safe and easy for everyone.
Doctor heals, teacher teaches, police keep us safe, farmer grows food.
Postman brings letters; firefighter puts out fires; sanitation workers keep streets clean.
Each helper uses special things and works in a special place.
Everyone at home can help — boys and girls, big and small.
Good friends share, take turns, help, say sorry and listen.
Helping words: Please help me. May I help you? Thank you.
In an emergency in India, call 112 and tell a grown-up.

rd-school-c1-english.unit-2-clean-fresh.title: Clean and Fresh: Bath Time
rd-school-c1-english.unit-2-clean-fresh.subtitle: Splash, scrub and smile — how we keep our bodies clean.

sections.md:
Do you like bath time? Water goes *splish*! Bubbles go *pop*!

Every day we take a **bath**. A bath washes away dust and sweat. After a bath we feel **clean** and **fresh**.

What do we need for a bath?

- a bucket of **water** 🪣
- a mug
- **soap** 🧼
- a **towel**
- clean clothes

**Say it:** *I take a bath every day.*

fig.caption: Bubbles float up at bath time.
fig.alt: A smiling child in a tub with bubbles rising.

check.q: What helps wash away dirt in a bath?
check.why: Soap and water together wash away dirt and germs.

sections.md:
Let us learn the steps of a bath. Act them out!

1. **Wet** your body with water.
2. **Rub** soap on your hands, arms, legs, neck and tummy.
3. **Scrub** behind your ears and between your toes.
4. **Rinse** off the soap with clean water.
5. **Dry** yourself with a towel.
6. Put on **clean clothes**.

These are **action words**: wet, rub, scrub, rinse, dry. Action words tell us what we do.

**Game — Simon says:** A grown-up says *Simon says rub your arms!* You rub. *Simon says dry your hair!* You dry. If the grown-up does not say *Simon says*, stand still!
keyTerms: rinse — wash off with clean water
towel — a soft cloth to dry the body

check.q: What do we do after rinsing off the soap?
check.why: After rinsing, we dry our body with a towel.

sections.md:
Bath time is not the only clean time!

- 🪥 **Brush** your teeth in the morning and at night.
- 🙌 **Wash** your hands before you eat and after you use the toilet.
- 💇 **Comb** your hair.
- ✂️ Keep your **nails** short and clean.

Germs are tiny. We cannot see them, but they can make us ill. Soap chases them away!

**How to wash hands:** wet, soap, rub palms, rub the backs, rub between the fingers, rub the thumbs, rinse, dry. Sing a short song while you rub — it gives the soap time to work.

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 220' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='220' fill='#f1f8e9'/><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='18' text-anchor='middle'><g><rect x='40' y='50' width='140' height='120' rx='16' fill='#fff' stroke='#8bc34a' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='70' y='100' width='80' height='14' rx='7' fill='#42a5f5'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='translate' values='-10 0;10 0;-10 0' dur='0.8s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></rect><text x='110' y='195'>brush teeth</text></g><g><rect x='230' y='50' width='140' height='120' rx='16' fill='#fff' stroke='#8bc34a' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='280' cy='110' r='22' fill='#ffcc80'/><circle cx='320' cy='110' r='22' fill='#ffcc80'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' values='-15 300 110;15 300 110;-15 300 110' dur='0.6s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle><text x='300' y='195'>wash hands</text></g><g><rect x='420' y='50' width='140' height='120' rx='16' fill='#fff' stroke='#8bc34a' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M450 80 h80 M450 80 v30 M465 80 v30 M480 80 v30 M495 80 v30 M510 80 v30 M525 80 v30' stroke='#795548' stroke-width='5'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='translate' values='0 0;0 30;0 0' dur='1.2s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path><text x='490' y='195'>comb hair</text></g></g></svg>
fig.caption: Three clean habits: brush, wash, comb.
fig.alt: Animated toothbrush, washing hands and a moving comb.

check.q: When should we wash our hands?
check.why: We wash hands before eating so germs do not go into our mouth.

sections.md:
Let us talk about our day. Say each line and do the action.

| When | What I do |
|---|---|
| 🌅 Morning | I wake up. I brush my teeth. I take a bath. |
| 🍛 Before lunch | I wash my hands. |
| ⚽ After play | I wash my face, hands and feet. |
| 🌙 Night | I brush my teeth. I go to sleep. |

**Talk time:** Ask a friend, *When do you take a bath?* Your friend says, *I take a bath in the morning.* Now swap!

Look at the words **morning** and **night**. They are opposites. Other opposites: **clean — dirty**, **wet — dry**, **hot — cold**.

check.q: What is the opposite of 'wet'?
check.why: A towel makes wet skin dry, so 'dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.

sections.md:
Some words sound alike at the end. They **rhyme**.

- *tub* — *rub* — *scrub*
- *soap* — *hope* — *rope*
- *clean* — *green* — *bean*

Make a little chant: *Rub, rub, rub in the tub! Scrub, scrub, scrub, no more mud!*

The letter **b** is in *bath, bucket, bubble*. Clap each time you hear the b sound.

**A little poem for you:**

> *Water warm and soap so white,*
> *Wash my face, I shine so bright.*
> *Towel soft and clothes so new,*
> *Clean and fresh — and you are too!*

check.q: Which word rhymes with 'tub'?
check.why: 'Tub' and 'rub' both end with the '-ub' sound.

sections.md:
Water is precious. In summer many towns in India get less water. So:

- Use a **bucket and mug**, not a running tap.
- **Close the tap** while you rub soap.
- Do not waste water while playing.
- Use leftover clean water for plants.

A clean child who saves water is a **super child**! 🦸

**Draw and colour:** Draw yourself after a bath. Draw a towel, a soap and a bucket next to you.

story.title: Bunty the Buffalo Who Loved Mud

parts.md: Bunty the baby buffalo loved mud. Squelch! Squish! He rolled in the mud all day by the village pond. His friends the ducks said, *Bunty, you look like a chocolate cake!*
One day Bunty's skin began to itch. *Scratch, scratch!* Mother Buffalo said, *Come, Bunty. Time for a wash.* She led him into the clear river water. Splash! The mud floated away.

Bunty came out shiny and fresh. The itch was gone. *Wow,* he said, *being clean feels good!* Now Bunty still plays in the mud — but every evening he takes a big, splashy bath. The ducks quack, *Bunty, now you shine like the moon!*

summary: We take a bath every day to be clean and fresh.
For a bath we need water, a mug, soap and a towel.
Bath steps: wet, rub soap, scrub, rinse, dry.
Brush teeth morning and night.
Wash hands before eating and after the toilet.
Germs are tiny and can make us ill; soap removes them.
Opposites: clean–dirty, wet–dry, morning–night.
Rhyming words: tub, rub, scrub.
Save water: use a bucket, close the tap.
practice: Name three things you need for a bath.
Say the bath steps in order.
When do you brush your teeth?
Say a word that rhymes with 'clean'.
Why should we wash our hands before eating?
Say the opposite of 'clean'.
How can you save water at bath time?

rd-school-c1-english.unit-3-pets.title: Pets and Animal Friends
rd-school-c1-english.unit-3-pets.subtitle: Woof, meow, moo! Meet the animals who live with us.

sections.md:
Some animals live in our homes with us. We call them **pets**.

- 🐶 a **dog**
- 🐱 a **cat**
- 🐟 a **fish**
- 🐰 a **rabbit**
- 🦜 a **parrot**

Some animals live on farms near us: the **cow**, the **goat**, the **hen**. They are our animal friends too.

**Say it:** *I have a pet. It is a ___.* Or: *I would like a pet ___.*

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 300' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='300' fill='#fff3e0'/><rect y='230' width='600' height='70' fill='#a5d6a7'/><g transform='translate(170,180)'><ellipse rx='70' ry='40' fill='#bc8a5f'/><circle cx='70' cy='-30' r='32' fill='#bc8a5f'/><ellipse cx='88' cy='-50' rx='10' ry='22' fill='#6d4c41'/><circle cx='80' cy='-35' r='5'/><circle cx='100' cy='-25' r='5' fill='#000'/><path d='M-70 -10 q-30 -30 -20 -50' stroke='#bc8a5f' stroke-width='10' fill='none' stroke-linecap='round'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' values='-15 -70 -10;20 -70 -10;-15 -70 -10' dur='0.5s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path><rect x='-50' y='25' width='14' height='35' fill='#bc8a5f'/><rect x='35' y='25' width='14' height='35' fill='#bc8a5f'/></g><g transform='translate(430,190)'><ellipse rx='50' ry='35' fill='#9e9e9e'/><circle cx='-45' cy='-35' r='28' fill='#9e9e9e'/><path d='M-68 -55 l8 -22 l10 18 z M-32 -58 l10 -20 l6 22 z' fill='#9e9e9e'/><circle cx='-55' cy='-38' r='4' fill='#2e7d32'/><circle cx='-37' cy='-38' r='4' fill='#2e7d32'/><path d='M50 0 q40 -10 30 -60' stroke='#9e9e9e' stroke-width='10' fill='none' stroke-linecap='round'><animate attributeName='d' values='M50 0 q40 -10 30 -60;M50 0 q10 -20 40 -50;M50 0 q40 -10 30 -60' dur='2s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path></g><text x='170' y='70' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='26' text-anchor='middle' fill='#6d4c41'>Woof!</text><text x='430' y='90' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='26' text-anchor='middle' fill='#555'>Meow!</text></svg>
fig.caption: A dog wags its tail and a cat swishes hers.
fig.alt: Cartoon dog with wagging tail and grey cat with moving tail.

keyTerms: pet — an animal that lives with us and we care for

check.q: Which of these is a pet that lives in water?
check.why: A pet fish lives in water in a bowl or tank.

sections.md:
Every animal has its own voice. Let us make the sounds!

| Animal | Sound |
|---|---|
| dog | woof woof |
| cat | meow |
| cow | moo |
| goat | baa |
| hen | cluck cluck |
| duck | quack quack |

**Game:** Your teacher says *moo*. You say *cow*! Your friend says *quack*. You say *duck*!

check.q: Which animal says 'moo'?
check.why: The cow says 'moo'.

sections.h: Where do they live? What do they eat?
sections.md:
Every animal needs a home and food.

| Animal | Home | Food |
|---|---|---|
| dog | kennel | food from our kitchen |
| fish | tank or bowl | fish food |
| parrot | cage or tree | fruits, seeds, chillies |
| cow | shed | grass, hay |
| hen | coop | grains |
| rabbit | hutch | carrots, leaves |

**Baby animals:** a baby dog is a **puppy**, a baby cat is a **kitten**, a baby cow is a **calf**, a baby hen is a **chick**, a baby goat is a **kid**.

**Say it:** *The puppy is small. The dog is big.*

check.q: What is a baby cat called?
check.why: A baby cat is called a kitten.

sections.md:
A pet is a friend who needs our care. A pet needs:

- 🍲 **food** every day
- 💧 fresh **water**
- 🏠 a safe, clean **home**
- 🤗 **love** and gentle hands
- 🩺 a visit to the **vet** (animal doctor) when it is ill

Never pull a dog's tail or a cat's ears. Be **gentle**. Also, wash your hands after playing with animals.

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='200' fill='#fce4ec'/><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='18' text-anchor='middle'><g transform='translate(100,90)'><ellipse rx='50' ry='18' fill='#e57373'/><ellipse cy='-6' rx='40' ry='10' fill='#ffb74d'/><text y='70'>food</text></g><g transform='translate(250,90)'><ellipse rx='50' ry='18' fill='#64b5f6'/><ellipse cy='-6' rx='40' ry='10' fill='#bbdefb'><animate attributeName='ry' values='10;6;10' dur='1.5s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></ellipse><text y='70'>water</text></g><g transform='translate(400,90)'><path d='M-40 20 v-40 l40 -30 l40 30 v40 z' fill='#a1887f'/><rect x='-12' y='-5' width='24' height='25' fill='#4e342e'/><text y='70'>home</text></g><g transform='translate(530,80)'><path d='M0 30 C-50 -5 -25 -45 0 -18 C25 -45 50 -5 0 30z' fill='#e91e63'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='scale' values='1;1.2;1' dur='1s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path><text y='80'>love</text></g></g></svg>
fig.caption: What every pet needs: food, water, a home and love.
fig.alt: Food bowl, water bowl, kennel and a beating heart.

check.q: Who is a vet?
check.why: A vet is a doctor who looks after animals.

sections.md:
Let us describe our animal friends.

- The elephant is **big**. The mouse is **small**.
- The rabbit is **soft**. The tortoise shell is **hard**.
- The cheetah is **fast**. The snail is **slow**.

These are **opposites**. Say them in pairs: *big–small, fast–slow, soft–hard*.

**Letter fun:** **d** for dog, **c** for cat, **p** for pet and parrot.

**Rhyme time:** *cat — hat — mat*, *dog — log — frog*, *hen — pen — ten*.

> *My little dog says woof all day,*
> *He wags his tail and wants to play.*

check.q: What is the opposite of 'fast'?
check.why: Fast and slow are opposites.

sections.md:
In Indian streets we see dogs, cows, goats and pigeons. They have no home of their own. In hot summer you can keep a bowl of **water** outside for birds and animals. Be kind, but keep a safe distance from animals you do not know. Ask a grown-up first.

**Did you know?** A dog can smell things many, many times better than we can!

**Make and do:** Make a paper mask of your favourite animal. Wear it and make its sound. Your friends guess the animal!

parts.md: It was raining. Under the stairs, Anu heard a tiny sound: *meeew*. It was a wet little kitten, shaking with cold. Anu ran to her grandmother. *Dadi, can we help?*
Dadi brought an old towel. Anu dried the kitten gently. They gave it a little milk-free food and a bowl of water. The kitten purred: *prrr, prrr*. *I will call you Motu,* said Anu.

Every day Anu filled Motu's water bowl and played with a ball of wool. When Motu sneezed, they took him to the vet. Soon Motu was big and strong. He followed Anu everywhere, like her shadow. *A pet is a friend,* said Dadi, *and a friend needs care.*

summary: Pets are animals that live with us: dog, cat, fish, rabbit, parrot.
Farm animals: cow, goat, hen.
Each animal has its own sound: dog woof, cat meow, cow moo.
Animals need homes: kennel, tank, shed, coop, hutch.
Baby animals: puppy, kitten, calf, chick, kid.
Pets need food, water, a home, love and a vet.
Be gentle; never hurt animals.
Wash hands after touching animals.
Opposites: big–small, fast–slow, soft–hard.
Keep water out for birds and street animals in summer.
practice: Name three pets.
What sound does a goat make?
What is a baby dog called?
Where does a hen live?
Say two things a pet needs.
What is the opposite of 'big'?
Who looks after sick animals?
Draw your favourite animal and say its name.

rd-school-c1-english.unit-4-birds-fruits.title: Birds and Fruits
rd-school-c1-english.unit-4-birds-fruits.subtitle: Tweet, tweet! Who is eating the mango?

sections.md:
Look up at the tree. Who is singing? It is a **bird**!

Birds have:

- two **wings** to fly
- **feathers** on their body
- a **beak** to eat
- two **legs**

Birds we see in India: the **parrot** 🦜 (green), the **crow** (black), the **sparrow** (small and brown), the **peacock** 🦚 (our national bird, with a beautiful tail), the **pigeon** (grey).

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 300' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><linearGradient id='k' x1='0' y1='0' x2='0' y2='1'><stop offset='0' stop-color='#4fc3f7'/><stop offset='1' stop-color='#e1f5fe'/></linearGradient></defs><rect width='600' height='300' fill='url(#k)'/><g><animateMotion path='M-80 150 C150 60 400 220 680 120' dur='7s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><ellipse rx='30' ry='16' fill='#43a047'/><circle cx='28' cy='-8' r='12' fill='#43a047'/><path d='M38 -8 l12 4 l-12 6 z' fill='#e53935'/><circle cx='31' cy='-11' r='2.5'/><path d='M-5 -5 q-15 -35 -30 -10 z' fill='#2e7d32'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' values='0;-30;0' dur='0.4s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path><path d='M-30 0 l-20 -6 l2 12 z' fill='#2e7d32'/></g><g transform='translate(480,250)'><rect x='-6' y='-20' width='12' height='70' fill='#6d4c41'/><circle cy='-50' r='50' fill='#66bb6a'/><circle cx='-20' cy='-40' r='10' fill='#ffb300'/><circle cx='22' cy='-55' r='10' fill='#ffb300'/></g><text x='300' y='40' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='26' fill='#01579b'>Tweet tweet!</text></svg>
fig.caption: A green parrot flaps its wings and flies to the mango tree.
fig.alt: A parrot flying across the sky toward a fruit tree.

keyTerms: beak — the hard mouth of a bird
feathers — soft covering on a bird

check.q: What does a bird use to fly?
check.why: Birds flap their wings to fly.

sections.md:
- The crow says **caw caw**.
- The sparrow says **chirp chirp**.
- The cuckoo says **koo-hoo**.
- The pigeon says **coo coo**.

Birds build **nests** with twigs, grass and leaves. Mother bird lays **eggs** in the nest. Baby birds come out of the eggs. They open their tiny beaks: *cheep cheep!* — they are hungry!

**Act it out:** Flap your arms like wings. Hop like a sparrow. Walk proudly like a peacock. Peck, peck, peck like a hen!

check.q: What does a bird build to keep its eggs?
check.why: Birds build nests of twigs and grass to keep their eggs safe.

sections.md:
Fruits are sweet and good for us. Let us name them and their colours.

| Fruit | Colour |
|---|---|
| mango 🥭 | yellow |
| banana 🍌 | yellow |
| apple 🍎 | red |
| grapes 🍇 | green or purple |
| orange 🍊 | orange |
| guava | green |

The **mango** is called the king of fruits in India. It comes in summer!

**Say it:** *I like apples. I like mangoes too.*

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><style>.p{animation:j 1.6s ease-in-out infinite;transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center}.p:nth-of-type(2){animation-delay:.3s}.p:nth-of-type(3){animation-delay:.6s}.p:nth-of-type(4){animation-delay:.9s}@keyframes j{50%{transform:translateY(-14px) rotate(6deg)}}</style><rect width='600' height='200' fill='#fffde7'/><g class='p'><ellipse cx='90' cy='100' rx='42' ry='55' fill='#ffb300' transform='rotate(-20 90 100)'/></g><g class='p'><circle cx='230' cy='105' r='45' fill='#e53935'/><rect x='227' y='50' width='6' height='16' fill='#5d4037'/></g><g class='p'><circle cx='370' cy='105' r='45' fill='#fb8c00'/></g><g class='p'><circle cx='490' cy='80' r='16' fill='#8e24aa'/><circle cx='515' cy='80' r='16' fill='#8e24aa'/><circle cx='502' cy='105' r='16' fill='#8e24aa'/><circle cx='478' cy='105' r='16' fill='#8e24aa'/><circle cx='490' cy='130' r='16' fill='#8e24aa'/></g><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='18' text-anchor='middle'><text x='90' y='190'>mango</text><text x='230' y='190'>apple</text><text x='370' y='190'>orange</text><text x='495' y='190'>grapes</text></g></svg>
fig.caption: Dancing fruits: mango, apple, orange, grapes.
fig.alt: Four bouncing fruits with labels.

check.q: Which fruit is called the king of fruits in India?
check.why: The mango is often called the king of fruits in India.

sections.md:
Use your senses to know a fruit!

- **Taste:** a mango is *sweet*. A lemon is *sour*. A raw guava can be a little *hard*.
- **Touch:** a banana is *soft*. A coconut is *hard*. A peach is *fuzzy*.
- **Shape:** an orange is *round*. A banana is *long*. A strawberry looks like a little *heart*.

**Inside a fruit:** cut it open (with a grown-up!) and look for **seeds**. A mango has one big seed. A watermelon has many small seeds. A banana has tiny seeds you can hardly see.

**Mystery game:** Close your eyes. A friend puts a fruit in your hand. Feel it, smell it — guess it!

check.q: Which fruit tastes sour?
check.why: A lemon has a sour taste.

sections.md:
Let us count!

- One mango 🥭
- Two bananas 🍌🍌
- Three apples 🍎🍎🍎

When there is more than one, we often add **s**: *one apple, two apples*.

**Letter fun:** **b** for bird and banana. **m** for mango. **a** for apple. **p** for parrot, peacock and pigeon.

**A little rhyme:**

> *One red apple, two bananas, three,*
> *Birds come flying to my mango tree!*

check.q: One banana, two ___.
check.why: For more than one banana, we add s: bananas.

sections.md:
Parrots love guavas and chillies! Many birds eat fruits and drop the seeds. New trees grow from those seeds. So birds help **plant** trees!

Be kind to birds: keep a bowl of water and some grains on your balcony in summer. Never throw stones at birds or break their nests.

**Did you know?** The peacock dances when the monsoon clouds come.

**Draw and colour:** Draw a tree with a nest and three fruits. Colour a bird sitting on it.

parts.md: In Nani's garden there was a tall mango tree. At the very top hung one last golden mango. Riya wanted it. Mithu the parrot wanted it too!
Riya stretched. Too high! She jumped. Too high! Mithu flew up and pecked the stem. *Tak!* The mango fell — *plop!* — right into Riya's hands.
Riya laughed. *Thank you, Mithu! Let us share.* She cut the mango. She ate one half. She put the other half on the wall for Mithu. *Tweet tweet!* said Mithu, which means *thank you* in parrot.

summary: Birds have wings, feathers, a beak and two legs.
Indian birds: parrot, crow, sparrow, peacock, pigeon.
The peacock is India's national bird.
Bird sounds: crow caw caw, sparrow chirp chirp.
Birds make nests and lay eggs.
Fruits: mango, banana, apple, grapes, orange, guava.
Mango is called the king of fruits.
Fruits can be sweet or sour, soft or hard, round or long.
Add s for more than one: apples, bananas.
Birds drop seeds and help new trees grow.
practice: Name two birds.
What does a crow say?
What colour is a parrot?
Name three fruits and their colours.
Name a sour fruit and a sweet fruit.
One apple, three ____.
Where do baby birds come from?
How can you help birds in summer?

rd-school-c1-english.unit-5-fun-fair.title: Fun at the Fair: Shapes and Play
rd-school-c1-english.unit-5-fun-fair.subtitle: Round wheels, square stalls, triangle flags — the fair is full of shapes!

sections.md:
Dhum-dhum! The drums are playing. It is the village **fair** — the **mela**!

At the fair we see:

- a big **giant wheel** 🎡 going round and round
- a **merry-go-round** with wooden horses
- **balloons** of every colour 🎈
- stalls with **bangles**, toys and sweets
- a **puppet show**

**Say it:** *I went to the fair. I saw a giant wheel.*

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 320' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='320' fill='#fff8e1'/><rect y='270' width='600' height='50' fill='#c5e1a5'/><g transform='translate(300,150)'><path d='M0 0 L-60 120 M0 0 L60 120' stroke='#795548' stroke-width='8'/><g><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' from='0' to='360' dur='10s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><circle r='100' fill='none' stroke='#e91e63' stroke-width='6'/><g stroke='#f48fb1' stroke-width='3'><line x1='-100' y1='0' x2='100' y2='0'/><line x1='0' y1='-100' x2='0' y2='100'/><line x1='-71' y1='-71' x2='71' y2='71'/><line x1='-71' y1='71' x2='71' y2='-71'/></g><g fill='#ffca28'><circle cx='100' cy='0' r='14'/><circle cx='-100' cy='0' r='14'/><circle cx='0' cy='100' r='14' fill='#42a5f5'/><circle cx='0' cy='-100' r='14' fill='#42a5f5'/><circle cx='71' cy='71' r='14' fill='#66bb6a'/><circle cx='-71' cy='-71' r='14' fill='#66bb6a'/><circle cx='71' cy='-71' r='14' fill='#ef5350'/><circle cx='-71' cy='71' r='14' fill='#ef5350'/></g></g><circle r='10' fill='#5d4037'/></g><g><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='translate' values='0 0;0 -20;0 0' dur='3s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><ellipse cx='80' cy='90' rx='22' ry='28' fill='#e53935'/><ellipse cx='520' cy='80' rx='22' ry='28' fill='#1e88e5'/><path d='M80 118 v80 M520 108 v80' stroke='#555'/></g></svg>
fig.caption: The giant wheel spins and the balloons float.
fig.alt: A spinning giant wheel with colourful seats and floating balloons.

keyTerms: fair / mela — a big outdoor gathering with rides, stalls and fun

check.q: Which ride goes round and round, high up in the sky?
check.why: The giant wheel turns in a big circle and lifts you high.

sections.md:
Look carefully. The fair is full of **shapes**!

- ⭕ **Circle** — the giant wheel, a bangle, a balloon from the front
- 🟥 **Square** — a box of sweets, a stall window
- 🔺 **Triangle** — the little flags, a samosa!
- ▭ **Rectangle** — a ticket, the tent door

A circle has no corners. A triangle has **3** corners. A square has **4** corners and all sides are the same.

**Make and do:** Cut circles, squares and triangles from coloured paper. Stick them to make a giant wheel, a tent and a flag line.

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 220' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><style>.s{animation:g 2.4s ease-in-out infinite;transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center}.s:nth-of-type(2){animation-delay:.6s}.s:nth-of-type(3){animation-delay:1.2s}.s:nth-of-type(4){animation-delay:1.8s}@keyframes g{50%{transform:scale(1.18)}}</style><rect width='600' height='220' fill='#f3e5f5'/><circle class='s' cx='85' cy='95' r='55' fill='#ec407a'/><rect class='s' x='175' y='40' width='110' height='110' fill='#42a5f5'/><polygon class='s' points='380,40 440,150 320,150' fill='#ffca28'/><rect class='s' x='470' y='60' width='110' height='70' fill='#66bb6a'/><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='20' text-anchor='middle'><text x='85' y='195'>circle</text><text x='230' y='195'>square</text><text x='380' y='195'>triangle</text><text x='525' y='195'>rectangle</text></g></svg>
fig.caption: Four shapes: circle, square, triangle, rectangle.
fig.alt: Pulsing circle, square, triangle and rectangle with labels.

check.q: How many corners does a triangle have?
check.why: A triangle has three sides and three corners.

sections.md:
Balloons, bangles, flags! Name the colours: **red, blue, yellow, green, pink, orange, purple**.

- *The balloon is red.*
- *The flag is yellow.*
- *The bangle is green.*

**Game — I spy:** *I spy something round and blue.* Your friend guesses: *A blue balloon!*

check.q: 'I spy something round.' Which could it be?
check.why: A bangle is round like a circle.

sections.md:
Some words tell us **where** things are.

- The giant wheel goes **up** and **down**.
- The puppet is **in** the box. Now it jumps **out**!
- The balloon is **above** my head. My shoes are **below**.
- The horse is **on** the merry-go-round. The dog sleeps **under** the stall.

**Big and small:** the giant wheel is **big**; the toy whistle is **small**. The rope is **long**; the ticket is **short**.

**Game:** Hold a ball. A friend says *up!* — lift it up. *Down!* — put it down. *Under!* — hide it under the chair.

check.q: The dog sleeps ___ the stall.
check.why: 'Under' tells us the dog is below the stall.

sections.md:
At the stalls we use **money**. In India we pay in **rupees** (₹).

- A balloon costs ₹5.
- A whistle costs ₹2.
- Two laddoos cost ₹10.

We say *please* when we ask and *thank you* when we get something.

**Talk time:**

- Child: *Please give me a red balloon.*
- Balloon seller: *Here you are. Five rupees, please.*
- Child: *Thank you!*

Act this with a friend. Use paper coins!

check.q: What do we say when someone gives us something?
check.why: Saying 'thank you' is polite when we receive something.

sections.md:
At the fair we **ride**, **clap**, **jump**, **laugh** and **eat**.

More play: we **run**, **hop**, **skip**, **throw** a ball and **catch** it.

Say with actions: *Jump, jump, jump! Clap, clap, clap! Hop, hop, hop!*

> *Round and round the wheel goes high,*
> *Up I go to touch the sky!*

**Staying safe at the fair:** Hold a grown-up's hand. If you get lost, stand still and tell a police officer or a stall uncle or aunty your parent's name and phone number.

check.q: If you get lost at a fair, what should you do?
options: Stand still and tell a safe helper
check.why: Staying in one place and telling a safe adult helps your family find you.

parts.md: Chintu went to the Diwali mela with Papa. Papa said, *Let us play a game. Find shapes!* Chintu looked around with big eyes.
*Circle!* — the giant wheel. *Triangle!* — the paper flags. *Square!* — the box of laddoos. *Rectangle!* — the ride ticket in Papa's hand. Chintu found ten shapes!

Papa bought him a balloon. *What shape is it?* asked Papa. Chintu thought hard. *From the front it looks like a circle!* They both laughed, rode the merry-go-round and went home with sticky jalebi fingers.

summary: A fair or mela has rides, stalls, balloons and shows.
The giant wheel goes round and round.
Circle: round, no corners.
Triangle: 3 sides, 3 corners.
Square: 4 equal sides, 4 corners.
Rectangle: 4 sides, 2 long and 2 short.
Colour words: red, blue, yellow, green.
Position words: up, down, in, out, on, under.
We pay in rupees and say please and thank you.
Play words: jump, clap, hop, run, ride.
At a fair, hold a grown-up's hand; if lost, stand still and tell a safe adult.
practice: Name four shapes.
Name something round at a fair.
How many corners does a square have?
Say three colours of balloons.
Use 'under' in a sentence.
How will you ask for a balloon politely?
Say three action words for play.
What will you do if you get lost?

rd-school-c1-english.unit-6-trees.title: Trees and Fruits
rd-school-c1-english.unit-6-trees.subtitle: Roots, trunk, branches, leaves — and sweet fruits to share.

sections.md:
Stand like a tree! Feet on the ground. Arms up high. Sway in the wind... *whoosh!*

A tree has parts:

- **Roots** — under the ground. They drink water.
- **Trunk** — the strong, thick stem.
- **Branches** — the arms of the tree.
- **Leaves** — green and flat. They make food from sunlight.
- **Flowers** and **fruits** — they grow on branches.

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 340' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='240' fill='#e1f5fe'/><rect y='240' width='600' height='100' fill='#8d6e63'/><g stroke='#5d4037' stroke-width='5' fill='none'><path d='M300 245 q-40 40 -90 60'/><path d='M300 245 q10 50 -10 85'/><path d='M300 245 q50 35 100 55'/></g><rect x='280' y='140' width='40' height='105' fill='#6d4c41'/><g><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' values='-3 300 240;3 300 240;-3 300 240' dur='4s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><circle cx='300' cy='110' r='85' fill='#43a047'/><circle cx='230' cy='130' r='50' fill='#4caf50'/><circle cx='370' cy='130' r='50' fill='#4caf50'/><circle cx='260' cy='100' r='10' fill='#e53935'/><circle cx='340' cy='90' r='10' fill='#e53935'/><circle cx='300' cy='145' r='10' fill='#e53935'/></g><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='18' fill='#222'><text x='440' y='60'>leaves</text><line x1='436' y1='55' x2='380' y2='80' stroke='#222'/><text x='440' y='130'>fruit</text><line x1='436' y1='125' x2='350' y2='95' stroke='#222'/><text x='440' y='200'>trunk</text><line x1='436' y1='195' x2='322' y2='195' stroke='#222'/><text x='440' y='300' fill='#fff'>roots</text><line x1='436' y1='295' x2='395' y2='298' stroke='#fff'/></g><path d='M300 330 v-80' stroke='#29b6f6' stroke-width='4' stroke-dasharray='8 10'><animate attributeName='stroke-dashoffset' values='0;-36' dur='1s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path></svg>
fig.caption: The parts of a tree. Water travels up from the roots.
fig.alt: A swaying tree labelled leaves, fruit, trunk and roots, with water moving up.

keyTerms: roots — parts under the ground that drink water
trunk — the thick, strong stem of a tree

check.q: Which part of the tree is under the ground?
check.why: Roots grow under the ground and take in water.

sections.md:
What do trees give us?

- 🍎 **fruits** to eat
- 🌬️ fresh **air** to breathe
- ⛱️ cool **shade** on a hot day
- 🪵 **wood** for doors and tables
- 🏡 a **home** for birds, squirrels and insects

In many Indian villages, people sit under a big **banyan** or **neem** tree to talk and rest.

check.q: Where do we sit on a hot sunny day?
options: in the shade of a tree
check.why: Trees give cool shade that protects us from the hot sun.

sections.h: Tall and short, big and small
sections.md:
Go outside and look at trees. Are they all the same? No!

- The **coconut** tree is **tall** and thin.
- The **banyan** tree is **big** and wide.
- A **tulsi** plant is **short** and small.
- **Rose** plants have **thorns** — touch gently!

Leaves come in many shapes and sizes. A banana leaf is **big** — in South India people eat meals on it! A tamarind leaf is very **small**. A peepal leaf looks like a **heart**.

**Leaf hunt:** Collect three fallen leaves. Which is the biggest? Which is the smallest? Put them in order from small to big.

**Colours of a tree:** green leaves, brown trunk, yellow mango, red flowers on the gulmohar in summer.

check.q: Which tree is tall and thin?
check.why: The coconut tree grows tall with a thin trunk.

sections.md:
Many fruits grow on trees:

| Tree | Fruit |
|---|---|
| mango tree | mango |
| coconut tree | coconut |
| banana plant | banana |
| guava tree | guava |
| jamun tree | jamun |

Inside many fruits there are **seeds**. Plant a seed, give it water and sunlight — and one day it can grow into a new tree!

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 220' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='170' fill='#fffde7'/><rect y='170' width='600' height='50' fill='#a1887f'/><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='16' text-anchor='middle'><g transform='translate(80,0)'><ellipse cx='0' cy='160' rx='12' ry='8' fill='#5d4037'/><text y='210' fill='#fff'>seed</text></g><g transform='translate(230,0)'><path d='M0 170 v-30' stroke='#388e3c' stroke-width='4'><animate attributeName='d' values='M0 170 v0;M0 170 v-30;M0 170 v-30' dur='4s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path><ellipse cx='-10' cy='140' rx='10' ry='5' fill='#66bb6a'/><text y='210' fill='#fff'>sprout</text></g><g transform='translate(380,0)'><path d='M0 170 v-70' stroke='#5d4037' stroke-width='6'/><circle cy='90' r='30' fill='#66bb6a'><animate attributeName='r' values='10;30;30' dur='4s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle><text y='210' fill='#fff'>plant</text></g><g transform='translate(520,0)'><rect x='-8' y='90' width='16' height='80' fill='#5d4037'/><circle cy='70' r='50' fill='#2e7d32'/><circle cx='-15' cy='70' r='7' fill='#ffb300'/><circle cx='18' cy='55' r='7' fill='#ffb300'/><text y='210' fill='#fff'>tree</text></g></g><path d='M110 120 H180 M260 120 H330 M420 120 H460' stroke='#ff7043' stroke-width='3' marker-end='url(#a)'/><defs><marker id='a' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='6' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0 0 L8 4 L0 8z' fill='#ff7043'/></marker></defs></svg>
fig.caption: From a tiny seed to a big fruit tree.
fig.alt: Growth stages: seed, sprout, small plant, fruit tree.

check.q: What can grow from a seed?
check.why: A seed with water and sunlight can grow into a new plant.

sections.md:
- **t** for tree and trunk
- **l** for leaf
- **r** for root

One leaf, many **leaves**. One branch, many **branches**.

Rhymes: *tree — bee — see*. *Leaf — thief*. *Root — boot — fruit*.

**Action rhyme:** *Roots go down, down, down. Branches go up, up, up. Leaves dance, dance, dance in the wind!*

**Talk time:** Ask your friend, *Which is your favourite tree?* Your friend says, *My favourite tree is the mango tree, because it gives sweet mangoes.*

check.q: Which word rhymes with 'tree'?
check.why: 'Tree' and 'bee' end with the same 'ee' sound.

sections.md:
We must take care of trees.

- Do not pluck leaves for fun.
- Do not write or carve on trees.
- Plant a sapling on your birthday!
- Water the plants at home and school.

**Did you know?** The banyan tree is India's national tree. Its branches send down roots that look like pillars!

**Draw and colour:** Draw a tree. Label the roots, trunk, branches, leaves and fruits.

parts.md: Long ago, Dada planted a tiny neem sapling near the school gate. Now it was big and tall. *Today is the tree's birthday,* said Teacher. *It is fifty years old!*
The children sat in its shade. A squirrel ran up the trunk. Two sparrows peeped from a nest. *The tree is a house for everyone,* said Rehan. *It gives us air and shade,* said Pooja.

How do you give a tree a birthday gift? The children poured water at its roots. They tied a ribbon around the trunk — gently. Then each child planted a new little sapling. The old neem tree rustled its leaves: *shhh-shhh*, like a happy thank you.

summary: A tree has roots, trunk, branches, leaves, flowers and fruits.
Roots drink water from the soil.
Leaves make food using sunlight.
Trees give fruit, air, shade, wood and homes for animals.
Trees can be tall, short, big or small; leaves have many shapes.
Mango, coconut, guava and jamun grow on trees.
Seeds can grow into new plants.
The banyan is India's national tree.
We should plant and protect trees.
practice: Name the parts of a tree.
Name three things trees give us.
Name a tall tree and a small plant.
Which fruit grows on a coconut tree?
What grows from a seed?
Say a word that rhymes with 'tree'.
Say one way to save trees.

rd-school-c1-english.unit-7-kites-sky.title: Kites, Wind and Sky
rd-school-c1-english.unit-7-kites-sky.subtitle: Up, up, up goes the kite — the wind is its friend!

sections.md:
On a windy day, the sky is full of **kites**! Red kites, yellow kites, kites with long tails.

A kite has:

- a light **frame** of thin sticks
- **paper** or cloth
- a long **string** (called *manjha* or *dor*)
- sometimes a **tail**

In Gujarat, people fly kites on **Makar Sankranti** (Uttarayan) in January. Everyone shouts *Kai po che!* when one kite cuts another.

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 340' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><defs><linearGradient id='sk' x1='0' y1='0' x2='0' y2='1'><stop offset='0' stop-color='#29b6f6'/><stop offset='1' stop-color='#e1f5fe'/></linearGradient></defs><rect width='600' height='340' fill='url(#sk)'/><g fill='#fff' opacity='.9'><g><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='translate' values='-100 0;650 0' dur='20s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><ellipse cx='60' cy='60' rx='50' ry='18'/><ellipse cx='90' cy='50' rx='30' ry='16'/></g></g><g><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='translate' values='0 0;20 -15;-10 10;0 0' dur='4s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><g transform='translate(420,100) rotate(15)'><polygon points='0,-55 40,0 0,65 -40,0' fill='#ef5350'/><line x1='0' y1='-55' x2='0' y2='65' stroke='#6d4c41' stroke-width='3'/><line x1='-40' y1='0' x2='40' y2='0' stroke='#6d4c41' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M0 65 q-15 20 0 40 q15 20 0 40' stroke='#ffca28' stroke-width='4' fill='none'><animate attributeName='d' values='M0 65 q-15 20 0 40 q15 20 0 40;M0 65 q15 20 0 40 q-15 20 0 40;M0 65 q-15 20 0 40 q15 20 0 40' dur='1s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path></g></g><path d='M420 165 Q300 250 140 300' stroke='#333' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'/><circle cx='130' cy='290' r='18' fill='#ffcc80'/><rect x='118' y='308' width='24' height='32' fill='#7e57c2'/><g stroke='#90caf9' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'><path d='M40 180 h80' stroke-dasharray='20 15'><animate attributeName='stroke-dashoffset' values='0;-70' dur='1s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path><path d='M60 210 h120' stroke-dasharray='20 15'><animate attributeName='stroke-dashoffset' values='0;-70' dur='1s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></path></g></svg>
fig.caption: The wind lifts the kite and its tail dances.
fig.alt: A red kite flying and swaying in a blue sky held by a child.

keyTerms: kite — a light frame with paper that flies on a string
string — a long thin thread

check.q: What helps a kite fly?
check.why: Moving air, the wind, pushes the kite up into the sky.

sections.md:
Kites come in many **colours** and **shapes**.

- Most kites look like a **diamond** — a square standing on one corner.
- Some kites are **triangles**. Some look like a **fish**, a **bird** or a **star**.

**Count the kites:** 🪁 one red kite, 🪁🪁 two blue kites, 🪁🪁🪁 three yellow kites. How many kites in all? Count: one, two, three, four, five, six — **six kites**!

**Big and small:** Papa's kite is **big**. My kite is **small**. The string is **long**. The tail is **short**.

**Say it:** *My kite is green. It is small. It flies high.*

check.q: One red kite and two blue kites. How many kites?
check.why: One and two more make three kites.

sections.md:
We cannot **see** the wind. But we can **feel** it on our face. We can see what it does:

- Leaves **flutter** and fall.
- Clothes on the line **flap**.
- Kites **fly** up high.
- A paper boat **sails** on a puddle.
- A windmill **spins**.

A soft wind is a **breeze**. A very strong wind is a **storm**. Go inside during a storm!

**Make and do — a paper windmill (firki):** Take a square of paper. With a grown-up, cut from each corner toward the middle (not all the way). Fold every other point to the centre and pin it to a stick. Run, or blow on it — it spins!

check.q: Can we see the wind?
options: No, but we can feel it
check.why: Wind is moving air; we cannot see it but we feel it and see what it moves.

sections.md:
Look up! In the sky we see:

**By day:** the **sun** ☀️, white **clouds**, birds, aeroplanes, kites.

**By night:** the **moon** 🌙 and twinkling **stars** ⭐.

Never look straight at the sun. It can hurt your eyes.

**Position words:** The kite is **up** in the sky. The boy is **down** on the ground. The bird flies **above** the tree. The cat sleeps **under** the tree.

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 220' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='300' height='220' fill='#81d4fa'/><rect x='300' width='300' height='220' fill='#1a237e'/><circle cx='150' cy='100' r='40' fill='#ffca28'/><g stroke='#ffca28' stroke-width='5'><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='rotate' from='0 150 100' to='360 150 100' dur='12s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><line x1='150' y1='40' x2='150' y2='20'/><line x1='150' y1='160' x2='150' y2='180'/><line x1='90' y1='100' x2='70' y2='100'/><line x1='210' y1='100' x2='230' y2='100'/></g><path d='M470 60 a40 40 0 1 0 30 70 a32 32 0 1 1 -30 -70z' fill='#fff9c4'/><g fill='#fff'><circle cx='350' cy='50' r='3'><animate attributeName='opacity' values='1;.2;1' dur='1.5s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle><circle cx='560' cy='40' r='3'><animate attributeName='opacity' values='.2;1;.2' dur='1.2s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle><circle cx='380' cy='160' r='3'><animate attributeName='opacity' values='1;.3;1' dur='2s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle><circle cx='540' cy='170' r='3'><animate attributeName='opacity' values='.3;1;.3' dur='1.7s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle></g><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='20' text-anchor='middle'><text x='150' y='210'>day</text><text x='450' y='210' fill='#fff'>night</text></g></svg>
fig.caption: Day sky with the sun; night sky with the moon and stars.
fig.alt: Split picture: sunny day and starry night with moon.

check.q: What do we see in the sky at night?
check.why: At night the moon and stars shine in the sky.

sections.md:
Action words: the kite goes **up**, **down**, **round** and **round**. We **pull** the string. We **run** with the kite. We **let go** of the string slowly.

Rhymes: *kite — white — night — bright*. *Sky — high — fly — my*.

**A little poem:**

> *Little kite, so light, so bright,*
> *Dance with the wind from morning to night.*
> *Up past the tree, up past the sky —*
> *Wave to the birds as you fly so high!*

**Safety:** Fly kites in an open field, far from electric wires and roads. Never climb on a roof edge for a kite. Glass-coated string can hurt people and birds — use plain cotton string.

check.q: Which word rhymes with 'sky'?
check.why: 'Sky' and 'high' end with the same sound.

sections.md:
**Talk time:** Ask a friend:

- *Have you flown a kite?* — *Yes, I have. / No, not yet.*
- *What colour is your kite?* — *My kite is orange.*
- *Where do you fly it?* — *I fly it in the park.*

**Draw and colour:** Draw the sky. Put a sun, two clouds, a bird and your own kite in it. Give your kite a long, wavy tail.

**Did you know?** Kites were first made very long ago in Asia. Some festival kites are so big that many people pull one string together!

parts.md: Pari made a kite from yellow paper and two thin sticks. Her brother's kite was big and red. *Mine is too small,* she sighed. *It will never fly.*
She ran across the field. No wind. The kite fell flop! She waited. Then — *whoosh!* — a breeze came. Up went the little yellow kite, higher than the neem tree, higher than the water tank!
*Look!* shouted Pari. *It is a tiny sun in the sky!* A bird flew past and looked at it curiously. Pari pulled the string gently and laughed. Small things can fly very high, if the wind is with you.

summary: A kite has a frame, paper, string and often a tail.
Kites come in shapes like diamonds and triangles and many colours.
The wind lifts the kite into the sky.
We cannot see the wind but we can feel it.
A soft wind is a breeze; a strong wind is a storm.
Day sky: sun, clouds, birds. Night sky: moon, stars.
Never look straight at the sun.
Position words: up, down, above, under.
Rhymes: kite–white, sky–high.
Fly kites in open fields, away from wires and roads.
practice: Name the parts of a kite.
What shape is most kites?
What does the wind do to leaves?
What do we see in the sky at night?
Say a word that rhymes with 'kite'.
Where should we fly kites?
Use 'up' and 'down' in a sentence.
Two kites and two more kites — how many kites?

rd-school-c1-english.unit-8-little-creat.title: Little Creatures
rd-school-c1-english.unit-8-little-creat.subtitle: Ants, butterflies, bees and snails — tiny friends with big jobs.

sections.md:
Bend down and look at the grass. What is moving? Little **creatures**!

- 🐜 **ant** — tiny and busy
- 🦋 **butterfly** — colourful wings
- 🐝 **bee** — buzz buzz, makes honey
- 🐌 **snail** — carries its house on its back
- 🐞 **ladybird** — red with black spots
- 🐛 **caterpillar** — long and wiggly
- 🕷️ **spider** — spins a web

fig.caption: A line of ants marches, a butterfly flutters, a snail rests.
fig.alt: Ants walking in a line, a butterfly flying, a snail on grass.

keyTerms: creature — any living animal, big or small
insect — a small creature with six legs

check.q: Which little creature carries its house on its back?
check.why: A snail has a hard shell on its back that is its home.

sections.md:
Look closely (with a magnifying glass if you have one).

| Creature | Legs |
|---|---|
| ant | 6 |
| bee | 6 |
| butterfly | 6 |
| ladybird | 6 |
| spider | 8 |
| snail | 0 — it slides on one soft foot |
| earthworm | 0 — it wriggles |

Creatures with **six legs** are called **insects**. A spider has **eight** legs, so it is *not* an insect!

**Where do they live?** Ants live in an **anthill**. Bees live in a **hive**. Spiders live on a **web**. Earthworms live in the **soil**. Snails hide under wet leaves and stones.

check.q: How many legs does a spider have?
check.why: A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect.

sections.md:
Little creatures have big jobs!

- **Ants** work together. They carry food much bigger than themselves, walking in a long line.
- **Bees** visit flowers and make **honey**.
- **Butterflies** fly from flower to flower.
- **Spiders** spin **webs** to catch flies.
- **Earthworms** live in the soil and keep it soft for plants.

When bees and butterflies visit flowers, they help plants make fruits and seeds.

check.q: Which creature makes honey?
check.why: Bees collect nectar from flowers and make honey.

sections.md:
Here is a magic change!

1. A butterfly lays a tiny **egg** on a leaf.
2. A hungry **caterpillar** comes out. It eats and eats leaves!
3. It wraps itself in a case called a **pupa** (or chrysalis) and rests.
4. Out comes a beautiful **butterfly**!

**Act it out:** Curl up small like an egg. Wiggle on the floor like a caterpillar. Wrap your arms around yourself and stay still like a pupa. Now open your arms wide and flutter — you are a butterfly!

fig.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 600 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect width='600' height='200' fill='#fffde7'/><circle cx='300' cy='95' r='80' fill='none' stroke='#ffb74d' stroke-width='3' stroke-dasharray='10 8'><animate attributeName='stroke-dashoffset' values='0;-36' dur='1s' repeatCount='indefinite'/></circle><g font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle'><g><circle cx='300' cy='15' r='9' fill='#fff' stroke='#999'/><text x='300' y='45' fill='#555'>egg</text></g><g><g><animateTransform attributeName='transform' type='translate' values='0 0;6 0;0 0' dur='0.8s' repeatCount='indefinite'/><circle cx='370' cy='95' r='7' fill='#7cb342'/><circle cx='382' cy='95' r='7' fill='#8bc34a'/><circle cx='394' cy='95' r='7' fill='#7cb342'/></g><text x='430' y='125'>caterpillar</text></g><g><ellipse cx='300' cy='178' rx='9' ry='16' fill='#a1887f'/><text x='360' y='190'>pupa</text></g><g><ellipse cx='212' cy='88' rx='10' ry='14' fill='#ab47bc'/><ellipse cx='228' cy='88' rx='10' ry='14' fill='#ab47bc'/><text x='180' y='125'>butterfly</text></g></g></svg>
fig.caption: The life cycle of a butterfly goes round in a circle.
fig.alt: A circle showing egg, caterpillar, pupa, butterfly.

check.q: What comes out of a butterfly's egg?
check.why: A caterpillar hatches from the egg and later becomes a butterfly.

sections.md:
- The bee **buzzes**: *bzzz*.
- The ant **crawls**.
- The butterfly **flutters**.
- The snail **creeps** slowly.
- The caterpillar **wiggles**.

**Small and tiny:** An ant is **small**. A dot is **tiny**. An elephant is **big**!

Rhyme: *bug — rug — hug*. *Bee — tree — free*.

> *Little ant, little ant, marching in a line,*
> *Carrying a crumb that is bigger than mine!*

**Be kind:** Do not step on ants on purpose. Watch insects, but do not catch butterflies — their wings are very delicate. Stay away from bee hives.

check.q: How does a snail move?
check.why: A snail creeps slowly on its soft body.

sections.md:
**Bug hunt:** Go into a garden with a grown-up. Look under a leaf, near a flower and on a tree trunk. Put a tick for each creature you see: ant ☐ bee ☐ butterfly ☐ snail ☐ spider ☐ ladybird ☐.

**Talk time:**

- *What did you see?* — *I saw a red ladybird.*
- *Where was it?* — *It was on a leaf.*
- *How many spots?* — *It had seven spots!*

**Draw and colour:** Draw a butterfly. Make both wings the same — if one wing has three dots, the other wing must have three dots too!

**Did you know?** An ant can carry things many times heavier than its own body.

story.title: Chiku the Ant and the Big Sugar Cube

parts.md: Chiku the ant found a sugar cube on the kitchen floor. It was huge — bigger than ten ants! *I will take it home alone,* he said. He pushed. He pulled. It did not move.
Chiku called his friends. One ant came. Two ants came. Ten ants came! *One, two, PUSH!* Together they lifted the sugar cube and walked in a long, neat line.
Back in the anthill everyone cheered. Grandma Ant said, *Little ones are strong when they work together.* That night every ant had a sweet dream.

summary: Little creatures: ant, bee, butterfly, snail, ladybird, caterpillar, spider.
Insects have six legs; a spider has eight legs.
Homes: anthill, hive, web, soil.
Ants work together and walk in lines.
Bees make honey; bees and butterflies help flowers make fruits.
Spiders spin webs.
Earthworms keep soil soft.
Butterfly life cycle: egg, caterpillar, pupa, butterfly.
Action words: buzz, crawl, flutter, creep, wiggle.
Be gentle with little creatures and stay away from hives.
practice: Name four little creatures.
How many legs does an ant have?
Where does a bee live?
What does a spider make?
Say the four stages of a butterfly's life.
How does a bee sound?
Why do ants walk together?
Say one way to be kind to little creatures.

rd-school-c1-english.unit-9-clouds-rainb.title: Clouds, Rain and Rainbow
rd-school-c1-english.unit-9-clouds-rainb.subtitle: Pitter-patter! Where does rain come from — and where do rainbows hide?

sections.md:
Look up. Do you see **clouds**? Some are white and fluffy like cotton. Some look like animals — an elephant, a rabbit, a fish!

When clouds become **dark** and **grey**, rain is coming. *Rumble, rumble!* That is **thunder**. *Flash!* That is **lightning**.

In India, the big rainy season is the **monsoon**. It comes in June and July and makes everything green.

**Cloud game:** Lie on the grass with a grown-up. Look at the clouds. Say what each one looks like: *That cloud looks like a camel!*
